events.title: The 23rd méxico now festival
events.description: nyc’s first and only independent festival spotlighting contemporary mexican art and culture returns with four days of panel discussions, book presentations, film screenings, and musical performances. various locations, free admission.

events.title: Mix nyc queer experimental film festival
events.description: the longest-running queer film fest in nyc returns with three nights of experimental films at bam rose cinemas and dixon place. $15+.

events.title: Quarter
events.description: A World Diabetes Day community screening of Quarter, a new film about life with type 1 diabetes, followed by a live Q&A with Kelsey Bascom, hosted by You're Just My Type. A pre-show meetup with Kelsey runs 5:00-6:00 PM for the first 20 RSVPs; the screening is at 6:20 PM. The $10 ticket is a donation to You're Just My Type. Rated R; 18+.

events.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
events.description: Times: 10am, 12:05pm, 5:20pm. John Turturro stars as Harry, an old-school New York hustler whose pickpocket take has shifted from cash and wristwatches to credit cards and cell phones, in Noah Segan's nostalgic portrait of a small-time criminal navigating a digitally networked world.

events.title: Club Kid in 35mm
events.description: Times: 10:15am, 1pm, 3:50pm, 6:45pm, 9:35pm. A hard-partying New York City club promoter sees his whirlwind lifestyle upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had. Written and directed by Jordan Firstman; screening in 35mm.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.description: Times: 10:45am, 3:10pm, 7:05pm, 9:50pm. Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

events.title: Mouse
events.description: Times: 10:50am, 3:55pm, 6:40pm. Opens Fri Nov 6 at IFC Center.

events.title: Paper Tiger in 35mm
events.description: Times: 11am, 1:40pm, 4:20pm, 7pm, 9:45pm. A 35mm presentation of James Gray's crime thriller set in 1986 New York, in which engineer Irwin (Miles Teller) and his ex-cop brother Gary (Adam Driver) are pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia after Irwin witnesses something at the Gowanus Canal.

events.title: Summer 2000: the X-Cetra Story
events.description: NYC premiere about four childhood friends who reunite in their 30s after a secret album they made as tweens is rediscovered. Screenings are followed by Q&As with members of the filmmaking team.

events.title: Wildwood in 35MM
events.description: Times: 12pm, 2:55pm, 5:50pm, 6pm, 8:45pm, 8:55pm. LAIKA's handcrafted epic fantasy in which a girl's desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into an adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, presented in 35mm.

events.title: Zhang Yimou's Raise the Red Lantern
events.description: Times: 12:20pm, 3pm, 5:40pm, 8:20pm. Zhang Yimou's RAISE THE RED LANTERN, now playing Friday, November 6 – Thursday, November 19.

events.title: A City in the Forest
events.description: NYC premiere about land defenders organizing against Atlanta's planned police training facility known as "Cop City." Screenings are followed by Q&As with co-directors Lev Omelchenko and Nolan Huber.

events.title: Understory
events.description: World premiere exploring plants as intelligent beings, with forester Suzanne Simard, botanist Robin Wall Kimmerer and philosopher Paco Calvo. The first screening will be followed by a Q&A with director Su Rynard and producer Nadine Pequeneza.

events.title: Soul Patrol
events.description: Thu Nov 5: Sneak preview + Q&A with dir. J.M. Harper at 7:30. Fri Nov 6: Q&A with dir. J.M. Harper at 7:15.

events.title: Gimme Truth
events.description: NYC PREMIERE Is it a conspiracy if it's true? From chemtrails to extraterrestrials, Gimme Truth explores how people from various backgrounds find themselves fixated by conspiratorial thinking.

events.title: Minotaur
events.description: Times: 2:15pm, 6pm, 8:45pm. Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Cannes Grand Prix winner: in Russia, 2022, corporate executive Gleb finds himself under siege at home and at work, where local authorities demand he draft employees for the war in Ukraine. In Russian with English subtitles; select open-caption showtimes.

events.title: Acting Like Women
events.description: NYC premiere revisiting the 1970s Los Angeles feminist art movement that culminated in the Woman's Building, with voices including Judy Chicago, Senga Nengudi, Suzanne Lacy and Lily Tomlin. The first and second screenings will be followed by a Q&A with Cheri Gaulke, Anne Gauldin and Kristy Tully.

events.title: Kikuyu Land
events.description: Times: 3pm, 3:30pm. Set in Kenya's tea highlands, Kikuyu Land follows Mr. Mungai, a local claimant pursuing justice for land taken from his family, as his fight brings him into conflict with a powerful multinational corporation. Q&A with Director/Producer/Film Subject Bea Wangondu and Producer Moses Bwayo on Nov 13 at 7pm, Nov 14 at 6:30pm and Nov 15 at 1pm; the Nov 19 3:30pm showing is also…

events.title: Hannah and Her Sisters - 35MM
events.description: 35mm screening of Hannah and Her Sisters (1986, 107 min): between three Thanksgivings, Hannah's husband falls for her sister Lee while her ex-husband rekindles things with her sister Holly.

events.title: Whiddy
events.description: World premiere about Gulf Oil's terminal on Ireland's Whiddy Island and the disastrous explosion that scarred the community, nominated in DOC NYC's inaugural Archival Storytelling Competition. The first screening will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers.

events.title: Amazing Live Sea Monkeys
events.description: NYC premiere about heiress Yolanda Signorelli von Braunhut's fight to steward the legacy of Sea-Monkeys. The first and second screenings are followed by Q&As with directors Mark Becker and Aaron Schock.

events.title: Landscapes of Memory
events.description: NYC premiere in which Leah Galant examines Germany's culture of memorializing the Holocaust while caregiving for her father as ALS takes his memory and speech. Screenings are followed by Q&As with members of the filmmaking team.

events.title: To the Lost Worlds – Uncovering the Secrets of the Guiana Shield
events.description: A series of seminars on the "Lost World" of South America's Guiana Shield.

events.title: Figaro Up, Figaro Down
events.description: NYC premiere about opera singer Tim Blevins, once destined for the world's grandest stages, who now sings on the streets while battling addiction and family estrangement. The first screening is followed by a Q&A with director Javid Soriano, producer Rob Richert and Tim Blevins.

events.title: What Happened to Danny
events.description: WORLD PREMIERE When 19-year-old Chinatown native Danny Chen dies while serving in Afghanistan, the official account raises troubling questions for the family who knew his ambitions and devotion to loved ones. As disturbing details surrounding his final weeks emerge, his grieving parents and New York community mobilize to uncover the truth.

events.title: Free Third Thursday Evenings: Art After Hours
events.description: Every third Thursday evening of the month, enjoy free admission to the Museum; browse the Shop; and sip wine, prosecco, beer, and cocktails alongside art and Central Park views. Free admission from 5 to 8 pm; tickets available online or at the admissions desk.

events.title: Broadway Under The Stars
events.description: Broadway Under The Stars, held on Thursdays from November 12th through December 17th.

events.title: Docent Tour: Lefor-Openo
events.description: A guided docent tour by the Poster House education team focusing on posters from Cuteness, Conservatism, & Consumption: Lefor-Openo and Postwar France. Admission must be purchased upon arrival to attend.

events.title: Recovering Histories on the Margins of Early Twentieth-Century NYC: A Panel Discussion Featuring Jonathan Ezra Goldman, Elena Martinez, Adam McKible, & Kara Schlichting
events.description: An author panel discussion focusing on early 20th century history. Panelists include Jonathan Ezra Goodman, Elena Martinez, Adam McKible, and Kara Schlichting.

events.title: MFA Fine Arts Fall 2026 Open Studios
events.description: Meet 59 artists from around the world pursuing an MFA in fine arts at SVA during the department's fall 2026 open studios, featuring work across a wide range of media and disciplines. Free with Eventbrite registration.

events.title: You don’t need a smartphone with august lamm
events.description: artist, writer, and anti-tech activist august lamm presents her practical guide to downgrading your phone and upgrading your life. rizzoli bookstore (flatiron), free admission.

events.title: México Now Festival 2026: Re and Beginning Middle End
events.description: Two México Now Festival book presentations: at 6pm (free, first come) a conversation on the 33 1/3 book about Café Tacvba's album Re, and at 7:30pm Valeria Luiselli and Charles de Montebello present her novel Beginning Middle End as a sonic experience. Registration required.

events.title: Uncertain Hours – Readings and Reflections in Poetry: Wanderlust and the Utopian Moment
events.description: Launch of a series of poetry readings with “Wanderlust and the Utopian Moment,” a reading by Norman Finkelstein, whose work explores childhood, diaspora, grief and elegy, history, Jewish mysticism, and mythology, joined in conversation by Mark Scroggins. Reservations are required: rsvp@primolevicenter.org (specify the program title).

events.title: FUTURES: An Anthology of Contemporary Arab Theater
events.description: Launch of FUTURES, an anthology of contemporary Arab plays in English translation, with NYC-based actors reading excerpts from three plays.

events.title: Élisabeth Jacquet de La Guerre: Lost Airs from Versailles — Concert Premiere
NYC Girlsgiving: Kitchen Table Talk Edition
Tár + Live Performance | Instruments of Desire
events.description: Screening of Tár (2022, 138 min) introduced by cultural critic Broey Deschanel, with the Candide Quartet performing Alban Berg's String Quartet, Opus 3.

events.title: A Better Way: James Lawson, Architect of Nonviolence
events.description: NYC PREMIERE The Rev. James Lawson was an unsung founder of the Civil Rights Movement who helped shape it through faith, moral clarity, and nonviolence. A close colleague of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., he later confronted racism, police violence, and apartheid.

events.title: Michelle Young : The art spy
events.description: The Art Spy, named a Best Book of 2025 by the New York Public Library, is a saga set in wartime Paris about how art historian Rose Valland infiltrated the Nazi leadership to save treasured masterpieces. Author Michelle Young will be in conversation with Julia Gamolina, founder of Madame Architect, covering the 1930s Paris avant garde, the secret lives of art historians in the French Resistance,…

events.title: Hermione Lee, Anita Brookner: Art and Life
events.description: Biographer Hermione Lee illuminates the life and work of novelist Anita Brookner.

events.title: This Is the Real World: Linda Condes and Karl Lagasse on Death Conquered and the Power of Hope
SKORTS, Paper Lady, Truman Flyer
events.description: Celebrate the new EP from SKORTS with Paper Lady and Truman Flyer, powered by Drops; free tickets with code DROPS and app download at the door. 18+.

events.title: Siri Hustvedt - Dance Around the Self
events.description: North American premiere portrait of writer Siri Hustvedt reflecting on literature, feminism, neuroscience, art, memory and her life with Paul Auster. The first and second screenings will be followed by a Q&A with director Sabine Lidl and Siri Hustvedt.

events.title: Noches de Cine: Un Poeta
events.description: Noches de Cine, El Museo's new film series celebrating the latest voices in Latine cinema, screens Un Poeta. Stay after the screening for conversation and community. Free.

events.title: Ethics and the Future of Reproduction: Making Eggs and Sperm from Skin Cells with Jeffrey Kahn and Anna Mastroianni
events.description: What if ordinary skin cells could be transformed into eggs or sperm? Scientists are exploring in vitro gametogenesis (IVG), a technology that could expand reproductive options while raising profound ethical questions.

events.title: Book Talk: The Realist: Hans Morgenthau and the Purpose of American Power
events.description: Author David M. Sacks in conversation with Gideon Rose. From $0.00.

events.title: Preserving Indigenous Music: Listening Session & Conversation with Justis Brokenrope and Sky Hopinka
events.description: Archivist Justis Brokenrope leads a vinyl listening session on American Indian and First Nations rock, folk, and country music. A conversation with artist and filmmaker Sky Hopinka explores Brokenrope’s archival work and the significance of Native music.

events.title: We Rise Up Singing: A Documentary Film by Peter Barton on the Brooklyn Women’s Chorus (Screening With Q&A)
artRINX Talks: Artists Discuss Works Priced Under $15,000
Live From New Amsterdam: The Ancient House — Erin Kramer on Albany as a Shared Space for the Dutch and the Haudenosaunee
Boatbuilders
events.description: Times: 6:30pm, 9:30pm. NYC premiere of Luke Lorentzen's portrait of craftsmen in a small Maine town building a 56-foot sailboat on commission. The first screening will be followed by a Q&A with director/producer Luke Lorentzen.

events.title: Modus @ Merkin: Celebrating America’s 250
events.description: Modus Operandi Orchestra celebrates America's 250th anniversary with a program of American music from Copland and Barber to Jessie Montgomery, culminating in Dvořák's New World Symphony.

events.title: Late Shift
events.description: Experience the Guggenheim after dark with art, music, drinks, and performances in the museum’s iconic spiral.

events.title: The Navigator
events.description: NYC PREMIERE As a young man, Nainoa Thompson became the first native Hawaiian in 600 years to voyage from Hawaii to Tahiti without the aid of modern instruments. 50 years later, he leads a new generation of student navigators on the 2,400-mile journey.

events.title: Soho Forum Debate: Noah Rothman vs. David Stockman — Is the U.S. War in Iran a War of Necessity?
The Wisdom Bar-"The Real Process Behind Writing a Novel: Author's Account"
Make Work
events.description: NYC premiere following choreographers during a 10-day creation process at the New York City Ballet's Choreographic Institute. Screenings are followed by Q&As with directors/producers Linda Saffire and Adam Schlesinger.

events.title: Helen Tworkov on Buddhism in America Across Generations
events.description: BPL Presents welcomes Helen Tworkov, founder of Tricycle: The Buddhist Review and author of Lotus Girl, for a conversation with a group of writers on Buddhism in America. Co-presented with Tricycle: The Buddhist Review.

events.title: The Broolyn Pancakes & Booze Art Show
events.description: Pancakes & Booze Art Show.

events.description: Brooklyn actor Jefferson White's directorial debut, about a diabetic running out of insulin who hitches a ride to Canada with his ex-fiancée and fellow healthcare refugees (1h22), followed by a Q&A. $25.

events.title: Trivia Night!
events.description: Trivia Night at Silvana hosted by Eric Lockley, with cool prizes, zero entry fee, and bragging rights. Doors open at 6:30, trivia kicks off at 7. Free.

events.title: Facts machine: science, comedy + trivia
events.description: scientists and comedians share the stories behind their favorite facts, ‘conduct experiments’ (i.e. play drinking games), and test their knowledge with a trivia challenge loosely inspired by this month’s theme: animal intelligence. hosted by scientists, comedians, and pub trivia hosts em costa, noah guiberson, and rob frawley. caveat (les), $13.61 with promo code ‘theskint’ (reg. $24-25).

events.title: Golden spiral comedy show
events.description: at mindy raf and katie compa’s golden spiral comedy show, stand-up set lengths follow the fibonacci sequence (5, 8, 13, and 21 minutes each). tonight’s show at whiskey cellar nyc (east village) features yemi afolabi (comedy central), jenn wehrung (bbc), kristal adams (netflix), missy baker (hbo), and chris castelli (shine box comedy). advance ticket purchase includes a raffle ticket for a free…

events.title: Carnegie hill concerts new-music chamber music series
events.description: the carnegie hill series wraps the fall season with an evening blending dream-folk, ambient, and experimental music with slowspin (sound artist zeerak ahmed). church of the advent hope (carnegie hill), choose-what-you-pay admission.

events.title: Nyc magic ensemble
events.description: expect the unexpected as the nyc magic ensemble presents a night of magicians and mentalists at young ethel’s (south slope), $10.

events.title: Immigrant Nation: Making a Library for Arts & Culture
Cinematic Correspondences: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha and Her Filmic Influences
events.description: Special screening presented with Artists Space's Theresa Hak Kyung Cha retrospective, featuring works by artists and filmmakers from her edited volume 'Apparatus' alongside Cha's own mid-1970s films, including PERMUTATIONS (1976).

events.title: All of a Sudden
events.description: Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto shared the Best Actress prize at Cannes for Academy Award–winning director Ryûsuke Hamaguchi’s (Drive My Car , NYFF59) radiant new film about a nursing home director promoting a radical new care program. Japan’s entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

events.title: Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing
events.description: NYC premiere following a new breed of sumo wrestlers training in Master Sakaigawa's Tokyo stable. The first screening will be followed by a Q&A with director Erik Shirai and producer Carolyn Hepburn.

events.description: A celebration of fantasy romance and Bramble authors, featuring a panel with Bramble authors Blake Blessing, Terry J. Benton-Walker, and RJ Valldeperas. This is a ticketed event.

events.description: SOLD OUT. The second-ever School Nite features live performances from lo-fi electronic R&B artist Nourished by Time and electronic multi-hyphenate Tromac, both from Baltimore.

events.title: Pete's Reading Series
events.description: Brooklyn’s premier literary series for over 20 years, Pete’s Reading Series features heavyweight authors side-by-side with rising stars. Curated by Brian Gresko and Temim Fruchter. Join us (for FREE!) on the third Thursday of every month.

events.description: 35mm screening.

events.description: A one-time special screening of Lupita Aquino-Kashiwahara's Once a Moth, starring Nora Aunor, in a newly restored edition courtesy of Kani Releasing, celebrating the new Pelikula76 zine on Filipino cinema. The zine's co-editors will introduce the film and sell copies of the zine.

events.description: Обычно мы оцениваем музеи по коллекциям, выставкам, удобству зданий или стоимости билетов, но каждый музей — это ещё и своего рода… Ukrainian, Russian and English bookshop in Prospect Heights (formerly MyBiblioteka): author talks, lectures and workshops, many in Russian.

events.description: Comedians will attempt (and most likely fail) to recreate "Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire" live onstage. Doors 7:30pm, show 8pm; 21+.

events.description: Landline Comedy from 8-9:30pm. Free.

events.description: Stevie Wonder will bring the Songs In The Key of Life Performances 50th Anniversary Tour to The Garden on November 19.

events.description: Low Cut Connie with Brian Dunne at Bowery Ballroom. Ages 18+, Doors Open 8pm, $30 Advance, $35 Day of Show.

events.description: NYC premiere celebrating Ken Cockrel, a radical lawyer in 1970s Detroit who won decisive victories in high-profile cases, nominated in DOC NYC's inaugural Archival Storytelling Competition. The first screening will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers and protagonists.

events.title: Pedro Giraudo Quartet
events.description: Argentine tango artist and Latin Grammy winner Pedro Giraudo performs with his quartet.

events.description: US premiere portrait of Shipibo artist Sara Flores, whose sacred geometries carry Indigenous knowledge from the Peruvian Amazon into museums worldwide. The first screening will be followed by a Q&A with directors Èlia Gasull Balada and Matteo Norzi and Sara Flores.

events.description: NYC premiere examining how corporations weaponize non-disclosure agreements, as three protagonists break their agreements. The first and second screenings are followed by Q&As with directors Miriam Shor and Juliane Dressner and protagonists.

events.description: NYC premiere following 10 young Ukrainians, ages 18 to 26, grappling with the impact of war. The first screening will be followed by a Q&A with director James Marcus Haney.

events.description: A 55-minute screening of 13 contemporary music videos by artists including Gucci Mane, Mitski, and Jihyo, followed by a Q&A. Presented by Hype Chateau.

events.description: A panel from the Zolberg Institute and the Center for the American Experience that takes the 1920s "Lippmann-Dewey debate" as a point of departure to consider democracy, public opinion, expertise, media, and political belonging in America today.
